item.title: Artificial photosynthesis uses waste CO₂ to grow protein-rich edible fungus in seven days
item.description: While many people think first of meat when they think about dietary protein, most protein ultimately depends on plants, since livestock feed on grass, hay and other plants. Meeting the demand for protein is taxing on the environment, requiring massive amounts of land and water while creating greenhouse gas emissions. And that demand is expected to require nearly 50% more agricultural production by 2050 than in 2012, according to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Without marine life, atmospheric CO₂ would shoot up by up to 65% by the end of the century
item.description: Without marine organisms transporting carbon into the deep ocean, the accumulation of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere would be drastically higher in the year 2100, reaching levels between 35% and 65% higher than projected. This is one of the main conclusions of the new policy brief developed within the framework of the European OceanICU project, which was presented at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Türkiye. Fuente: Phys.org.

La situación en el terreno sigue siendo muy compleja: aún hoy hay familias que buscan a sus desaparecidos entre los escombros. Nuestra corresponsal Daniella Zambrano nos amplió la información. item.title: Ancient Cahokia transformed amid droughts and flooding—climate change is reshaping modern communities in similar ways
item.description: More than 800 years ago, a combination of environmental and societal challenges led some Mississippian people to leave Cahokia, a massive archaeological site that was once home to 20,000 people near modern-day St. Louis. Just south of Cahokia, another archaeological site is taking shape at Centreville, Illinois, as modern-day people abandon their homes in the face of 21st-century climate and cultural changes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Turns out bumblebees are spontaneous problem solvers too! In a series of experiments, scientists found that untrained bumblebees were able to find novel solutions to get a reward. The research builds on previous experiments that showed that bumblebees can work as a team and possess cognitive abilities despite their tiny brains. Watch this video to […] Fuente: Mongabay.
